html:
SMTO-POL-0032 — Something SMTO found has changed since it looked

GUID: be9c0291-3207-5ed2-b623-bfb5a98dcc22
Slug: resource-identity-changed
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • Between finding an item and asking you about it, something about the item or its settings changed, so SMTO can't be sure the question would be accurate. No question was shown and no access was given.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a message asking SMTO to look up the items again and then ask for permission. A fresh lookup records the item's current details, which the permission question must match.
  2. If you recently updated or reconnected a Gateway, check it is connected again in Settings › Setup › Gateways before asking. Updating or reconnecting a Gateway makes earlier lookups on that computer out of date.
  3. If you recently changed Skills or permission settings, wait until those changes are saved, then ask SMTO to look again. A Skill or permission change made while SMTO was working also makes its earlier lookup out of date.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a new permission card for the item, and you can answer it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve an older card for this item, and don't ask anyone to turn off these safety checks to make the request go through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • request_resource_access was rejected because at least one discovered resource failed revalidation of its tool or Skill contract digest, Gateway contract digest or authority revisions, or had invalid metadata.

What this means

  • Before publishing consent, the controller revalidates the frozen discovery candidates against current tool contracts, resource boundaries and authority revisions. Missing or invalid metadata also fails this check. The diagnostic does not identify a specific policy change or prove that a resource was removed.

Why this can happen

  • Before publishing consent, the controller revalidates the frozen discovery candidates against current tool contracts, resource boundaries and authority revisions. Missing or invalid metadata also fails this check. The diagnostic does not identify a specific policy change or prove that a resource was removed.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare fresh discovery with the previous resource identity, tool contract and policy revisions.

How to fix it

  • Re-run discover_resources and request the fresh references. Possible causes are a changed tool or Skill contract, a Gateway whose contract changed after an update or re-registration, or changed authority or policy revisions; the result does not say which, and does not prove the resource was removed.
  • Discover the resource again, inspect its current identity and request only the access needed for this task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry the permission request only with freshly validated discovery references.

How to verify the fix

  • Freshly discovered resources pass validation before a new permission question appears.

What not to do

  • Do not approve stale identities or disable identity validation to make the request pass.

Technical notes

  • Validation rejects the request before a new permission question or grant is committed.
  • The result does not distinguish deletion, reconfiguration, policy revision or invalid metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
